14.	X was a major world religion founded in the 3rd century CE by an Iranian prophet after whom the religion is named. It taught an elaborate dualistic cosmology describing the struggle between a good spiritual word of light, and an evil material world of darkness. The founder deliberately set out to integrate, succeed, and surpass what he viewed as the “partial truths” of various prior faiths including Platonism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, Buddhisim, Judaism, Gnosticism, and various Mesopotamian belief systems. Some forms of X viewed its founder as the final prophet after Zoroaster, Buddha, and Jesus. At its height, it was one of the world’s most widespread religions, with churches from China to Iberia, and before the advent of Islam, the main rival to early Christianity.
